measurements.notes: MEASURED on this machine: full screen 1920x1080 -> 2765 tokens on a high-res model (no API downscale: 2.07 MP < 3.588 MP cap), 1534 on legacy tier (downscaled to ~1430x804). So on plain 1080p the high-res tier already DOUBLES the per-look cost vs the reference 1280x800 viewport (1366) — before any high-DPI hardware is involved. THE WINDOWS-SPECIFIC POINT, which inverts the macOS framing: display SCALING (100/125/150%) does not change capture cost here — Windows screenshots are physical pixels, and physical resolution is scale-invariant on a given panel (unlike macOS, where a Retina 'viewport screenshot' doubles with backing scale). What scaling DOES break on Windows is COORDINATES (UIA rects are physical px; a DPI-unaware client works in virtualized px — the classic blind-click trap; this machine at 96 DPI cannot exhibit it, stated honestly; all probes here were per-monitor-DPI-aware as the brief mandates). The cost trap moves to PANEL resolution: computed with the exact two-tier formula — QHD 2560x1440 -> 4784 highres / 1534 legacy; 4K 3840x2160 -> 4785 / 1534 (naive w*h/750 would claim 11060 — off by 2.3x, same class of error the macOS campaign caught). Structured views are resolution- AND scale-invariant (Notepad view: 502 tok at any DPI). Practical reading for a Windows fleet: on the common 1080p desktop the structured/pixels ratio for a full-screen look is 2765/view; on a 4K laptop it is capped at ~4785/view on high-res models and collapses to 1534/view on legacy models because the API throws the extra pixels away.
